title: Trail of Tears: forced removal of the Cherokee
summary: From May 1838 US troops and state militia rounded up the Cherokee in Tennessee, Alabama, North Carolina and Georgia, evicting more than 16,000 people. After Principal Chief John Ross negotiated with General Winfield Scott, Cherokee-led detachments travelled west between August and December 1838, and relocation was complete by March 1839. NPS says more than 1,000 died on the trip; Elizur Butler estimated over 4,000 deaths.

uncertainty.note: NPS pages give differing counts of detachments (13, 14, 17) and of deaths; see reviewer_note.

importance.justification: A forced march of more than 16,000 Cherokee that killed thousands and remains central to US-Native history.

audience_note: Describes the forced removal of the Cherokee people, including round-ups at gunpoint, family separation, and the deaths of children and elders from disease and exposure. It is told mainly from US National Park Service and Cherokee-focused sources; a Cherokee Nation or Eastern Band source should be added when it is expanded.

reviewer_note: Numbers: NPS trte says over 16,000 evicted, more than 1,000 died on the trip, perhaps several thousand more from consequences; NPS Little River Canyon gives Butler's estimate of over 4,000; the NPS Fort Smith page gives over 10,000 across all removed nations (not used). Detachment counts differ across pages (13, 14, 17); omitted. Cherokee agency: Ross petitioned Scott and supervised the detachments (Native History Association; Cherokee Trilogy says each was led by a Cherokee conductor); the Cherokee Nation and Eastern Band (about 1,000 avoided the roundup, per NPS) have not been consulted directly. Mantle Rock year 1839.0 is inferred (NPS gives January and says all survivors reached the West by March 1839). Tahlequah Aug 1839 is from NPS Little River Canyon. Tahlequah degrees-minutes-seconds converted to decimal. Only one non-NPS publisher with a government class was not found; all non-NPS sources are class other.

beats.caption: In June 1838 the first detachments leave Ross's Landing under military escort, after troops had rounded up Cherokee into stockades from May.
Cherokee-led detachments walk west from August to December 1838; ice on the Ohio and Mississippi halts the last one.
More than 1,000 are counted dead on the trip; a missionary doctor estimated over 4,000 deaths in all. Ross is chosen chief of the rebuilt nation in 1839.
